section_summary: This section finishes recommendations for military government control of Japanese production, including personnel policy, preservation of records, reporting, allocation of materials, and regional administration. It then supplies a table of administrative regions and appendices translating or summarizing Japanese wartime laws and industrial control arrangements. The final appendix sets out rules for a Hokkai warehouse control association.

subfiles.title: Recommendations for military government administration of Japanese production
subfiles.about: The concluding recommendations propose how military government should direct production and use Japanese economic institutions.
subfiles.summary: The report recommends encouraging democratic producer cooperatives while abolishing wartime Control Societies, excluding senior wartime officials from service, and protecting industrial records and property. It proposes detailed factory and prefectural reporting, material allocations tied to cooperation, and central and regional production control agencies to meet occupation and civilian needs.

subfiles.title: Appendix I: Administrative Regions of Japan—1945
subfiles.about: A table lists Japan's administrative regions, constituent prefectures, and regional headquarters as of June 1945.
subfiles.summary: Lists regional districts, prefectures, and headquarters.

subfiles.title: Appendix II: National Mobilisation Law of Japan
subfiles.about: The translated law defines national mobilization and grants the Japanese government extensive wartime control powers.
subfiles.summary: The law defines mobilization goods and businesses and authorizes control of labor, production, trade, finance, facilities, prices, publications, research, and industrial organizations. It provides for expropriation, compensation, inspection, penalties, and a National General Mobilisation Commission. The appendix cites a 1941 published collection of wartime legislation.

subfiles.title: Appendix III: Major Provisions of the Munitions Company Act
subfiles.about: An abstract outlines state direction and supervision of designated munitions companies.
subfiles.summary: The act requires designated firms to meet government munitions plans, appoint production officers, and comply with orders on labor, materials, facilities, finance, and corporate operations. It also provides for inspection, assistance, profits, and penalties.

subfiles.title: Appendix IV: Activities of the Munitions Superintendence Bureaus of the Ministry of Munitions
subfiles.about: The abstract describes the organization and operation of regional bureaus supervising munitions production.
subfiles.summary: It identifies bureau locations and sections, explains their unified control of capital, labor, materials, power, and production, and discusses overlapping authority with companies, local administrations, and the armed services. It reports that 424 munitions companies were placed under bureau supervision. The cited source is dated June 11, 1944.

subfiles.title: Appendix V: Major Industries Organization Ordinance
subfiles.about: The ordinance establishes and regulates industrial Control Societies and district Control Associations.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines the membership, officers, powers, financing, reporting duties, and government supervision of Control Societies and Control Associations. It authorizes these bodies to direct production and distribution, inspect members, impose assessments and fines, and enforce control regulations. Later provisions address military matters and application in overseas territories.

subfiles.title: Appendix VI: Amendments to the Essential Industries Organizations Law
subfiles.about: The appendix sets out amendments expanding the duties and administrative powers of industrial control associations.
subfiles.summary: The amendments add planning, purchasing, marketing, accounting, welfare, inspection, and registration provisions for control associations. They also address deputies, dismissal of obstructive officers, and changes to existing articles.

subfiles.title: Appendix VII: Transfer of Administrative Authority Law
subfiles.about: The law transfers specified government licensing and allocation powers to industrial control organizations.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes delegated powers and officials' legal responsibility.

subfiles.title: Appendix VIII: Metal Industry Control Society
subfiles.about: The abstract describes the Metal Industry Control Society's membership, committees, and plans for controlling metal production and supplies.
subfiles.summary: Established in January 1942, the society coordinated metal producers through committees dealing with materials, finance, technology, labor, and South Seas policy. It inventoried supplies, planned distribution and technical standards, studied working conditions, and awaited approval of its control regulations. The cited source was published in 1943.

subfiles.title: Appendix X: Control Regulations concerning Control Association of Hokkai Warehouse Enterprises
subfiles.about: The regulations prescribe reporting, management, labor, storage, and rate controls for member warehouse enterprises.
subfiles.summary: Members must submit business and financial information, report operational changes, and follow association directions on facilities, goods, labor, and storage contracts. The association may allocate storage, transfer goods among members, regulate wages, and set storage rates. The text states that the regulations took effect on June 20, 1944.
